name: Sanity
look: Nocturnal command centre — 112px display type with extreme negative tracking, pure achromatic greys, coral CTA against electric-blue hover.

hero.title: Content is data
hero.sub: Lexicon treats your content as a queryable dataset with a schema you define in code, not as pages in a database you cannot reach.

features.title: A backend your editors can actually use
features.sub: Schema in code, a real query language, and an editing surface you can bend to the team using it.

items.title: Schema as code
items.body: Content types are TypeScript objects in your repository, versioned and reviewed like everything else you ship.

items.title: A query language
items.body: Ask for exactly the shape your component needs in one request, with joins, filters and projections.

items.title: Real-time editing
items.body: Multiplayer editing with presence and per-field history, so two editors on one document is normal rather than a conflict.

items.title: Content releases
items.body: Stage a set of changes across many documents and publish them together at a scheduled time.

items.title: Asset pipeline
items.body: Uploads are transformed on request — crop, format, quality — with a CDN in front and no build step.

items.title: Everything is an API
items.body: The editing environment is a React application you own. Add a field, a widget or a whole workflow.

showcases.title: Ask for the shape you need
showcases.body: One request returns exactly the fields your component renders, joined across references, filtered and ordered. No over-fetching, no assembling three responses in the client, no waiting on a backend team to add an endpoint.
points: Joins and projections in a single query
Typed results generated from your schema
Live queries that push updates over a socket

showcases.title: Governance without a second system
showcases.body: Roles are defined per document type and per field, audit history is retained for every change, and content can be pinned to a region for residency requirements.
points: Full audit history with per-field diffs

gallery.title: Documentation
gallery.sub: Reference, guides and starter templates for every framework we support.

testimonial.quote: The editors stopped filing tickets asking us to change a field label, because they can change it themselves now. That is a strange thing to put in a case study and it is also the whole return on the migration.
testimonial.name: Nora Fitzgerald

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.sub: Free while you build. Usage-based once you are live.

items.a: The editing environment is a React application that runs anywhere you like. The content backend is a hosted service; a self-hosted backend is available on Enterprise agreements only.
By API requests and stored documents. Queries served from the CDN cache do not count, which for most production sites is the large majority of traffic.

items.q: What happens to our content if we leave?
items.a: Export the full dataset as newline-delimited JSON plus the original assets, at any time, from the CLI. There is no proprietary format to unpick.

items.q: Does it work with our framework?
items.a: There are typed clients for JavaScript, Python, PHP, Go and Swift, plus a plain HTTP API. Nothing about the platform assumes a particular front end.

cta.title: Start building
cta.sub: Free while you build, and no card required to create a project.

footer.tagline: Structured content infrastructure for teams that treat content as data.

notes: The near-black canvas is the identity, not a dark mode. There is no light counterpart to design.
Display type runs to 112px with roughly -4% tracking. That compression is the brand voice — do not loosen it to be safe.
The grey ramp is strictly achromatic. Introducing a warm or cool grey undoes the discipline the whole system rests on.
Coral is the CTA; electric blue is the hover state for every interactive element. They are two roles, not two accents.
IBM Plex Mono carries code and technical labels, giving the editorial display type a developer counter-register.
